rv.q: Kinky Boots director Jerry Mitchell and book writer Alexander Dinelaris do a very decent job with this bio-musical.

The second act become more ballad-heavy - perhaps unavoidably given the narrative. After a horrific tour bus collision, Gloria has titanium rods put in her back and needs months of gruelling physio to get on her feet again. But still, there are moments when you might wonder when the rhythm is gonna ...
Estefan ballads such as Anything For You, Don't Wanna Lose You and Are sound as soupy and samey as they did on the radio.

Had the show been mounted in a dance-friendly, hang out and slurp mojitos kind of venue, it might succeed in spicing up the audience's summer with the infectious rhythms of Estefan's pop-Latin fusions.
The only gem in a treasure chest of fool's gold was Karen Mann as Gloria's pushy grandmother Consuelo nailing some rare gags with her knowing looks and cheeky demeanour.
